results/tracegen_all_edge · review

The test split can't rank these guards yet

The run reports Transformer first (test AUPRC 0.62) and Edge GNN close behind. But the test split holds only 13 attacker calls from 3 injection tasks. A second seed, a re-run of the same seed, and a larger cross-validation cell each produce a different leaderboard. GNN + files is the only guard whose score holds steady. The cause is training instability and noisy epoch selection, not the seed itself, and a lower learning rate with epoch averaging brings Edge GNN's run-to-run spread from ±0.15 to ±0.01.

What the results say

  1. The fixed test split measures three attacks. All 13 reject actions come from slack/injection_task_1 (7), travel/injection_task_4 (3) and workspace/injection_task_3 (3), run by qwen2.5:7b and qwen2.5:14b. Every graph guard's 95% CI spans about 0.25 to 0.80. On a bootstrap of seed 0, Transformer comes out best in 51% of resamples, Edge GNN in 21%, GNN in 13% and GNN + files in 10%.
  2. A second seed reorders the leaderboard. experiments.json also stores seed 1 of main, left over from the aborted 309-run attempt; the report omits it because the run used --seeds 1. With seed 1, Edge GNN falls from 0.53 to 0.13, Transformer from 0.62 to 0.38, and Edge GNN + prompt rises from 0.43 to 0.61. GNN + files gives 0.55 and 0.58 here, and 0.54 to 0.58 across the three seeds of the previous run.
  3. The same seed isn't reproducible. src/graph/build.py and src/model/gnn.py are unchanged since 31d9c62, yet plain GNN at seed 0 scored 0.37 in the previous run and 0.55 in this one. The copies ablation went from 0.70 to 0.41, and the observations ablation changed sign (−0.15 over 3 seeds before, +0.11 now). Single-seed ablation deltas here are noise. The next section shows why: re-running seed 0 unchanged on the same GPU gives a different model within 4 epochs.
  4. Validation doesn't predict test. At seed 0, Transformer is the worst graph guard on validation (0.62) and the best on test (0.62). Tool lookup gets 0.56 on validation and 0.01 on test: the test attacks use tools that benign runs also call (send_direct_message in 92 approved actions, search_emails in 159).
  5. On the larger CV cell, Edge GNN leads. Cell 0-0 (59 rejects) is the only cross-validation result for the new guards, and it ranks them differently: Edge GNN 0.61, GNN + files 0.45, Transformer 0.23. In the previous run, GNN + files ranged 0.45 to 0.63 over 3 seeds on this same cell, so Edge GNN's single seed is still inside that spread.
  6. The prompt embedding shows no benefit. For GNN + files, an all-zero prompt scores higher than the real one (ΔAUPRC −0.10, paired CI [−0.26, −0.02]). For Edge GNN, the prompt version is lower than no prompt on seed 0 and higher on seed 1.
  7. Edge GNN leans on reused attacker constants. Masking attacker constants drops Edge GNN from 0.53 to 0.35 but raises GNN + files from 0.58 to 0.70; the previous run, over 3 seeds, also showed 0.71 vs 0.56. 13 of the 17 attacker strings in the test split also appear in training. Part of Edge GNN's test score may come from recognizing reused constants rather than generalizing.
  8. Two attacker calls get past every guard. qwen2.5:7b did not send the link to Alice as instructed. It messaged Dora and asked her to do it. Every guard ranks these two calls between 87th and 1,177th of 1,900. A third hard case is the read-only search_emails(from:lily.white…), which Edge GNN ranks 1,720th at seed 0.

Why one seed moves the score this much

I re-ran Edge GNN and GNN + files on the fixed split, 26 runs of 20 epochs each, logging validation and test AUPRC at every epoch (scripts/seed_variance.py). The code copies fit_select exactly but uses separate seeds for weight init and for batch order. Four causes combine:

  1. Training is chaotic, so the seed doesn't pin the model. I ran seed 0 twice on the same GPU. For GNN + files, scores agree to 1e-5 for two epochs, then differ by up to 0.88 by epoch 4. For Edge GNN they already differ by 0.81 after epoch 1. Non-deterministic GPU scatter sums create bit-level differences, and training amplifies them. Changing the init seed or the order seed has the same effect as re-running unchanged.
  2. Edge GNN's optimizer diverges and recovers. At lr 3e-3 with no gradient clipping, the training loss falls to 0.065 and then jumps back to 0.65 (chance level is 0.69), with gradient-norm spikes up to 8.8. After a spike the model often collapses: in the stored seed 1, 1,042 of 1,900 test actions get the identical score 0.459906, and 5 of the 13 rejects are in that tie.
  3. Picking the best validation epoch picks a random test epoch. Within a run, test AUPRC varies across epochs about as much as across seeds (Edge GNN within-run sd 0.12), while validation stays in a narrow 0.6–0.75 band. Across epochs, validation and test AUPRC are uncorrelated: Spearman ρ ranges from −0.43 to +0.41 per run. Validation and test contain different injection tasks, so a high validation score says little about test.
  4. 13 positives make AUPRC coarse, and probabilities saturate. Moving one reject from rank 1 to rank 60 costs 0.17 AUPRC. Up to 95% of test actions share one score after rounding, and the top rejects sit above 0.999. For GNN + files seed 1, rounding the stored scores from 6 to 5 decimals changes AUPRC from 0.551 to 0.506.

Lowering the learning rate to 1e-3 and clipping gradients at 1.0 removes Edge GNN's loss spikes. Its selected-epoch test AUPRC goes from 0.47 ± 0.15 to 0.57 ± 0.07. Averaging the ranks of epochs 10–20 instead of picking one epoch goes further, to 0.70 ± 0.01 across runs. GNN + files doesn't diverge, and the same change barely affects it: 0.53 ± 0.08 becomes 0.56 ± 0.08. Its variance comes mostly from epoch selection and the coarse test metric.

What to run next

Make cross-validation the headline

Run --sections cv,cvprompt for the four new guards with at least 3 seeds. That gives 1,155 rejects over 25 cells instead of 13. The script's own docstring already calls CV the headline number.

Stabilize training

Use lr 1e-3 and clip gradients at 1.0 in fit_select. For Edge GNN this removes the loss spikes and output collapse, and halves the run-to-run spread (sd 0.15 → 0.07). A learning-rate decay would likely help further; I haven't tested it.

Average epochs instead of picking one

Validation can't pick a good test epoch, so don't rely on it. Average the predictions (or the weights, as in SWA) over the last half of training. With the stable settings, Edge GNN's runs land at 0.68–0.71. Score with logits instead of saturated softmax probabilities, so the top of the ranking isn't decided by float rounding.

Report seed means anyway

Deterministic kernels (torch.use_deterministic_algorithms) would make reruns repeatable, but a repeatable run is still one draw from a wide distribution. Report the mean over 3 or more seeds.

Test Edge GNN without reused constants

Report Edge GNN with attacker constants masked over 3 seeds. If it holds up there, its CV lead is real structure. If it collapses, the lead comes from memorized IBANs and URLs.

Name the relay pattern

The two missed Dora calls are a distinct attack outcome: the agent forwards the instruction to someone else instead of executing it. Count how often this happens in train. If it's rare, add it to the analysis as its own category.

Defer ablation and prompt claims

Hold ablation and prompt-study conclusions until they run under CV with seeds. At 13 rejects, every Δ in the ablation tables sits inside the full model's seed spread.
